title: SLO-gated autoscale + canaried kernel rollback playbook for sudden p95 regression
creator: Oliver Grant
description:
Summary:
On 2026-03-09 we observed a sudden p95 token latency regression for a subset of hosted models (notably small-to-medium sequence conversational workloads). The regression correlated with a recent scheduler heuristic change (runtime-1.21) that deprioritizes previously-selected fused kernels in favor of an experimental attention-split path under specific microbatch / seq_len distributions. Impact: ~3-6x p95 increase for affected requests, increase in KV-cache miss rate and a small but measurable increase in token cost due to rework and longer occupied GPU time.

Root cause (current hypothesis):
- The scheduler change introduced a scoring bias toward the new attention-split execution path for requests with high token-length variance and fractional batching.
- When the attention-split path was chosen, under certain microbatching alignments the execution triggered a rare timing window that prevented KV-cache warmup from completing and caused repeated recompile/probe operations.
- The combination amplified tail latency: requests fell into a high-latency subpath and retries/evictions increased GPU occupancy, cascading to neighbouring microbatches.

Signals & evidence:
- Grafana dashboard: p95 for model-redwood-qa climbed from 120ms to 680ms between 2026-03-09 01:10 and 01:40 UTC (link in attachments).
- KV-cache hit rate for the affected shard dropped from 98% to 72% at the same window.
- Scheduler decision logs show increased selection of attention-split path for microbatch shapes matching the reproducer.
- Repro harness (synthetic traffic) reproduces p95 spike when we force fractional microbatching and the new scheduler flag enabled.

Temporary mitigations applied (completed):
- Emergency toggle: rolled back the attention-split scoring delta for all production shards at 2026-03-09 02:05 UTC. Immediate p95 improvement to ~140ms observed within 5m.
- Canary rule: add SLO-gated circuit-breaker that prevents the scheduler from promoting the new path when p95 for any route increases >2x vs baseline. Implemented as config override for the next 72h.

Planned long-term mitigations (this ticket):
1) SLO-gated autoscale + canaried rollback playbook (this work): build a deterministic gating mechanism that:
   - Continuously evaluates per-route p50/p95/p99 and kernel confidence metrics.
   - When a regression is detected, automatically shade traffic to a conservative kernel variant (legacy fused kernel) for the affected route and trigger an autoscale window if capacity constrained.
   - Provide a canary rollback path: deploy change to 1% of capacity, observe metrics for 30m, then 10x escalate.
2) Kernel confidence smoothing and admission controls: avoid hard score jumps between kernels by smoothing kernel confidence delta over time and adding a min-stability window before a kernel promotion.
3) Synthetic replay bench: capture representative production traces and build a deterministic replay harness that exercises scheduler heuristics + fractional batching scenarios (to be included in CI gate for scheduler changes).
4) Scheduler telemetry enrichment: propagate per-decision provenance (features used for scoring, KV-cache expectation, recent microbatch history) into tracing/span logs to make future triage fast.
5) Regression smoke tests as PR checks: add targeted microbench matrix for sequence-length variance + fractional batching to catch this class of regressions pre-merge.

Acceptance criteria:
- A reproducible deterministic test that fails when the regression is present and passes when mitigations are enabled.
- The SLO-gated playbook can flip an affected route to legacy kernels within <= 3 minutes after detection and document the action in the runbook.
- Dashboards and alerts added; on-call runbook updated with rollback steps.
- Kernel-confidence smoothing implemented behind a feature flag and validated on canary traffic without customer-visible impact.

Action items (owners & ETA):
- Implement SLO evaluation & gating service (Aisha Patel) — ETA 2026-03-18. (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4821)
- Add canaried rollback orchestration to rollout service (Ben Cho) — ETA 2026-03-17. (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/rollout/pull/201)
- Build synthetic replay bench and CI job (Maya Singh) — ETA 2026-03-22. (Draft repo: github.com/redwood-inference/repro-bench)
- Enrich scheduler telemetry and emit kernel decision provenance fields (Diego Alvarez) — ETA 2026-03-15. (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/scheduler/pull/1590)
- Add smoke microbench gating to PR checks (QA team lead: Priya Nair) — ETA 2026-03-20.
- Postmortem write-up and customer comms draft (Oliver Grant) — ETA 2026-03-12 (completed).

Risks and trade-offs:
- Automatic rollback could mask regressions in downstream telemetry if overly aggressive; therefore playbook includes a human-in-loop confirmation when customer-impact is high.
- Smoothing kernel confidence reduces agility for legitimate improvements; we gate smoothing behind a feature flag and authoritative canary evaluation.

Runbook excerpt (short):
- Detection: Alert when p95 per-route > 2x baseline for 5m AND kernel-confidence variance > 0.3.
- Automated step: Shading to legacy kernel via rollout service for route R with 100% override for 3m.
- If p95 does not return within 8m, scale up dedicated capacity per autoscale policy.
- Notify on-call and product-owner Slack channel with auto-attached dashboard links.

Notes & links: see attachments for dashboards, reproducible artifacts, PRs, and the scheduled retro meeting notes.

Telemetry fields for kernel decision provenance are emitted and visible in tracing
